history.summary: A Krishna temple at No. 5, Sardar Kulbir Marg, Railway Road, New Industrial Township-5, Faridabad (the temple's own site is bihariji.org). Devotional listings describe it as a 'Sidh Sthaan' of Lord Krishna, but no published founding date, builder or consecration record was found (UNVERIFIED); the 'ancient' claim on devotional listing pages is unsourced. It is one of Faridabad NIT's better-known temples (around 4.5-5.0/5 across listings) and is distinct from the famous Banke Bihari temple of Vrindavan.

name: Shree Banke Bihari Mandir
town_description: Faridabad is Haryana's largest city and a major industrial hub on Delhi's southeastern edge, part of the Delhi NCR. It was founded in 1607 by Shaikh Farid (Mughal emperor Jahangir's treasurer) as Farid's town. The NIT (New Industrial Township) area, developed in the 1950s for Partition refugees, is one of its oldest planned quarters; NIT-5 sits close to the railway line and Railway Road.

travel.railway: Faridabad Railway Station - about 0.9 km (verify); Neelam Chowk Ajronda Metro Station - about 0.5 km (verify).
travel.road: Railway Road, No. 5, Sardar Kulbir Marg, New Industrial Twp 5, NIT Faridabad, Haryana 121001; near Old Faridabad, reachable by auto and taxi.

visitor_information.best_time: Janmashtami for the grandest celebrations; October to March for pleasant weather.
